subject: Model fit evals & parity next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit evals & parity next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for a great conversation this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side: 

1) Recap of discovery
- Main goal: replace parts of PayGrid's proprietary NLP pipeline with a lower-cost, maintainable inference stack while keeping quality at or near your current baseline for merchant classification and invoice parsing.
- Key constraints: PII-handling requirements, 99.9% availability during business hours, and median latency targets under ~350ms for typical requests.

2) Proposed model-fit evaluation (mutual action plan)
- Scope: Run model-fit evals on a 2k-example holdout set focused on merchant classification, line-item extraction, and short-form Q&A. We can do this with either (a) a redwood-managed sandbox where you upload obfuscated data, or (b) synthetic dataset derived from a small sample you provide.
- Metrics: accuracy / F1 (primary), hallucination rate (secondary), and latency percentiles. For parity discussions we typically use 90–95% of your proprietary baseline as the initial acceptance band depending on metric and criticality.
- Recommended models to test (shortlist):
  * redwood-13b-q4 (cost-effective, tuned for classification/structured extraction)
  * open-llama-70b-qlora (higher capacity open model with quantization tradeoffs)
  * redwood-70b-fp16 (higher performance baseline we run for comparison)

3) Deliverables from Redwood
- Prompt set (attached: prompt-set-v1.txt) and evaluation harness with reproducible metrics.
- Preliminary benchmark results and notes (link below).
- SOC2 report and deployment options summary (private VPC/on-prem available).

4) Next steps / asks
- Can you confirm which option you prefer for the eval data (sandbox upload vs. synthetic)?
- Do you have any non‑negotiable parity thresholds (e.g., F1 >= 0.95) or are you comfortable starting at the 90–95% band?
- Possible times for a 30‑minute kickoff next week: Wed 3/31 9:30–11:30am PT or Thu 4/1 1:00–3:00pm PT.

I’ve attached a short recommendations PDF and the prompt set to get started. If that all sounds good I’ll loop in Marissa to scope the evaluation runbook and coordinate environment/access.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-model-recommendations.pdf, prompt-set-v1.txt
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Samantha Ruiz <s.ruiz@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & parity next steps

Thanks Lauren — solid recap, appreciate the clarity. A couple quick questions from my side: 

- Compliance: we will need to see your SOC2 report and a high-level data flow diagram showing how PII is masked in the sandbox. Is the SOC2 link public or can you share a PDF?
- Data: PayGrid prefers to avoid sending production PII. We’re interested in the synthetic route unless you can guarantee irreversible obfuscation in the sandbox. Can you outline the obfuscation approach briefly?
- Pricing: can you provide a rough order-of-magnitude estimate for (a) the eval run (2k examples across 3 models) and (b) monthly cost projections if we move to dedicated capacity for 50 req/s?

If folks are available I can do the kickoff Wed at 10:00am PT (that fits my calendar).

–Alex
Alex Chen | Head of ML Engineering, PayGrid
alex.chen@paygrid.com

On Tue, Mar 30, 2027 at 10:15 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks again for a great conversation this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side: ...
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Samantha Ruiz <s.ruiz@paygrid.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & parity next steps

Thanks Alex — quick answers inline and a bit more detail to unblock the kickoff.

- SOC2: Link here (public PDF): https://app.redwood.com/reports/soc2-2026.pdf. We’ll also share a short attestation that covers sandbox obfuscation controls.

- Obfuscation approach: for sandbox uploads we run a one‑way tokenization + entity substitution pipeline (PII replaced with realistic placeholders) and store only the tokenized data in the sandbox. If you prefer never to leave your environment, we can provide an on‑prem ingestion script that runs the same transformations and returns a synthetic dataset to our eval harness.

- Pricing (rough estimates):
  * Eval run (3 models x 2k examples): ~$1,200 — this covers GPU time and engineer support for setting up the harness and producing the report.
  * Dedicated capacity (50 req/s, mixed LLMs): ballpark $25k–$35k/month depending on model selection and quantization profile; we can produce a detailed cost model once we finalize target latency and batch settings.

- Recommended parity thresholds (proposal for discussion):
  * Merchant classification: F1 >= 0.92 vs. your baseline
  * Line-item extraction (span-level): exact match >= 0.88
  * Hallucination rate for Q&A: <= 3% on targeted prompts
  * Latency: median <= 350ms for the production configuraton

- Preliminary benchmark: I’ve uploaded a short CSV with our internal pre-runs comparing redwood-13b-q4 vs open-llama-70b-qlora vs redwood-70b-fp16 — link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/paygrid-2027 (preview) and attached paygrid-benchmark-results.csv. These are synthetic runs to set expectations only.

If you’re good with Wed 3/31 10:00am PT I’ll send the invite and Marissa will pick up the eval runbook and access steps.

Best,
Lauren

Attachments: paygrid-benchmark-results.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & parity next steps (internal)

Lauren — noted on the kickoff at 10:00am PT. I’ll prepare the eval runbook and make sure the sandbox obfuscation steps are documented. A couple internal items to track before kickoff: 

- Confirm which models we want to include in the first run (I recommend redwood-13b-q4 and open-llama-70b-qlora; hold 70b-fp16 as optional depending on PayGrid approval).
- Pre-check: ensure SOC2 share link and an internal copy of the obfuscation script are in the ticket.
- I'll draft the acceptance criteria sheet with the thresholds Lauren proposed and add a short section on regression monitoring: we should capture prompt-level deltas and make a plan for post-deploy quality alerts if parity slips >5% on key prompts.

I'll bring the runbook and attachments to the kickoff.

—Marissa

marissa@redwood.com
